To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MCB approach is able to detect chromosome aberrations with a higher resolution than G banding, that it can be applied to clinical cases, and that it can be performed on interphase nuclei.
the combination of MCB, FISH, and CGH is an excellent approach to characterise the breakpoints of chromosome rearrangements in a high resolution and reliable manner.
the use of region specific FISH and MCB probes in combination allows the detection and characterisation of all types of structural chromosome aberrations with high resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the chromosomal origin and the precise localisation of chromosome rearrangements in clinical cases.

the development of a new FISH technique that can be applied to all chromosomes and chromosome arms and that is capable of detecting chromosome aberrations with a resolution of about 5 megabases (Mb) or 1.5 million base pairs.

the development of new molecular cytogenetic methods that allow the detection of chromosome aberrations at the highest possible resolution and that can be easily integrated into routine cytogenetic laboratories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of MCB and region specific FSH probes is the most suitable method for the precise characterisation of chromosome aberrations in human cytogenetic diagnostics.
all these techniques have their own advantages and disadvantages, which have to be taken into account when selecting a method for the analysis of a certain chromosome aberration.
M-FISH, SKY, MCB, and RX-FISH are complementary and can be used in parallel to improve the characterisation of chromosome aberrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an FISH technique that is capable of detecting chromosome breakpoints with a resolution of 5–10 Mb and that can cover the entire human genome with human DNA probes.

we have developed a technique that can be used for the characterisation of chromosome rearrangements and/or chromosome abnormalities in clinical cases, and that we have developed probes for the identification of chromosome 2 aberrations.

the use of the high resolution MCB technique has led to the identification of new chromosome rearrangements, which were not detectable by conventional banding methods and/or by other molecular cytogenetic methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of MCB and FISH probes can help to solve the most difficult cases of chromosome aberrations.
the use of MCB in combination with region specific FISH is an efficient tool for chromosome identification and characterisation of chromosome aberrations in clinical specimens.

we have developed a novel technique that is able to identify the exact location of chromosome breakpoints and can be used to characterise complex chromosomal rearrangements in a fast and reliable way.
